title: Filter conditions: typed enums instead of String (filenode role/nodeType, notification type, task progress)
description:

## FileNodeFilterCondition.role and .node_type are String although NodeRole and NodeType exist; diverges from mail canonical
Crates: jmap-filenode-types (consumed by jmap-chat-filenode-server, jmap-filenode-server)
Evidence: crate-jmap-filenode-types/src/filter.rs:62 `pub node_type: Option<String>`, filter.rs:66 `pub role: Option<String>`. The object fields are typed: filenode.rs:296 `pub role: Option<NodeRole>`. `NodeRole` (filenode.rs:56) and `NodeType` (filenode.rs:18) are #[non_exhaustive] with an Other catch-all, so typing loses nothing. The canonical mail-types types the same filter: crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs:250 `pub role: Option<Option<MailboxRole>>`. The chat binding has to stringify by hand at crate-jmap-chat-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:151 and :357 (`filter.role = Some(NodeRole::ChatSpace.to_wire_str().to_owned())`), and a backend translating the filter to SQL has to re-parse the string to compare with the typed column. Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-16.txt:823 `nodeType: "String"`, :830 `role: "String" — A role name. Only nodes with precisely this role match`. These are the same value sets as the object's `role`/`@type`. Not covered by JMAP-wf92.25 (comparators only) or JMAP-v9py.16.1 (spaceId).
Why breaking later: Changing a public field type on a published struct is a break for every caller that sets or reads it (the struct is #[non_exhaustive], so callers mutate fields directly, as both binding sites do).
Fix: Make `role: Option<NodeRole>` and `node_type: Option<NodeType>` (serde already round-trips both through their wire strings), and update filenode-server memory.rs filter matching and the two chat-filenode-server call sites.

## Filter conditions take String where the object property is a typed enum (Notification type, Task progress)
Crates: jmap-calendars-types, jmap-tasks-types
Evidence: calendars-types/src/notification.rs:90 `notification_type: NotificationType` vs filter :248 `notification_type: Option<String>`. tasks-types/src/notification.rs:67 `NotificationType` vs filter :145 `Option<String>`. tasks-types/src/task.rs:484 `progress: Option<TaskProgress>` vs filter :593 `progress: Option<String>`. The established sibling pattern reuses the object enum in the filter: mail canonical EmailFilterCondition.has_keyword: Option<Keyword> (mail-types/src/query.rs:139), and sharing PrincipalFilterCondition.type_: Option<PrincipalType> (sharing-types/src/principal.rs:163). draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06.txt:1197 says "The type property must be the same".
Why breaking later: Changing the type of a public field on a public filter struct is a semver break, and builders written against String would stop compiling.
Fix: Use Option<NotificationType> (both crates) and Option<TaskProgress> in the filter conditions. All three enums already carry Other(String), so no expressiveness is lost.

## Filter conditions use String where the object field and the mail canonical use the typed enum (FileNode nodeType/role, CalendarEventNotification and TaskNotification type)
Crates: jmap-filenode-types, jmap-calendars-types, jmap-tasks-types
Evidence: crate-jmap-filenode-types/src/filter.rs:62 `pub node_type: Option<String>` and :66 `pub role: Option<String>`. The object fields are typed: filenode.rs:209 `node_type: Option<NodeType>` and :296 `role: Option<NodeRole>`, both #[non_exhaustive] enums with Other(String). crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/notification.rs:248 and crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/notification.rs:145 have `pub notification_type: Option<String>`, but the object field (calendars notification.rs:90, tasks notification.rs:67) is `NotificationType`, which also has Other(String). The canonical, crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs:250, types its filter as `pub role: Option<Option<MailboxRole>>` although RFC 8621 says that filter is "String|null". jmap-chat-types query.rs:96 does the same (`kind: Option<ChatKind>`). The specs word these filters the same way: draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-16.txt:823 `nodeType: "String"` and :830 `role: "String"`; draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33.txt:2709 `*type*: String`; draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06.txt:1197 `*type*: String`. That is the same wording as the mail case, so the typed shape is not ruled out by the spec. Typing the filter with the object enum loses nothing, because Other(String) round-trips unknown values. The AGENTS.md filter-algebra exclusion forbids adding extra fields or Other variants to filter conditions; it does not forbid reusing an existing result enum, and mail already does that.
Why breaking later: Changing a pub field's type from Option<String> to Option<NodeType>, Option<NodeRole> or Option<NotificationType> breaks every caller that builds or matches these filter structs. It also breaks the server-side filter code that compares strings. After 0.4 this needs a major bump on three types crates and their servers. Today the client compiles a filter like `nodeType: "dir"` with no help from the type system, while the object type next to it is typed.
Fix: Change FileNodeFilterCondition.node_type to Option<NodeType> and .role to Option<NodeRole>, and NotificationFilterCondition.notification_type and TaskNotificationFilterCondition.notification_type to Option<NotificationType>, following MailboxFilterCondition.role. Update the memory-backend matchers in filenode-server, calendars-server and tasks-server to compare enums or as_str(). Add a round-trip test from a spec-example JSON filter.
Size: S
